note: WebKit's browser install pulled packages from Ubuntu's mirror until the job timed out.
Firefox stayed on the runner apt install, and that install later timed out.
Putting the label on each option registration rendered the list again when labels changed.
The auto-scroll edge sat under the sticky stage names, so a drop near the start of the day missed.
readThumbSize returned early when the user agent said jsdom, so the shipped package behaved differently under test.
The end input's box started at the start thumb and painted later, so its track covered that thumb and the empty track differed on the two sides.
Each range input was only as wide as its thumb and handled the drag itself, so the gesture mapped across no travel and the value collapsed.
The pointer mapped across the full group, so a press on the drawn thumb moved the value by half the thumb.
The thumb was left to accent-color. WebKit does not paint the thumb from that, so Safari kept the native white thumb.
The server root wrote --_value once, so the single fill stayed put in Chromium and WebKit while the thumb moved.
The thumb test read an empty computed style and fell back to the stylesheet rule, and it never looked at the Firefox thumb.
The single fill used clip-path shape() and overflow-inline, which Chrome 128 through 134 do not have, so the thumb shadow painted a block over the page.
appearance none replaced the native thumb and the disabled state kept the fill color, so a disabled slider looked enabled.
